correctness.rationale: The binary divisor zeta transform is an exact ring isomorphism from each divisor-supported finite subring to a product of local square-zero \(\mathbb F_2\)-rings. Each principal ideal in a local factor is zero, the whole factor, or a two-element nilpotent line; all pairwise meets are principal. For any larger divisor cutoff, the images of the two elements and the proposed generator retain scalar flags and radical-vector comparisons (with extra zeros), so the equality extends to the directed union. Exactly 139536 ordered finite pairs were independently enumerated in six subrings; these tests corroborate but do not establish the unbounded proof. An explicit ring quotient shows the stronger all-ideals-principal assertion is false. Four exhaustive finite embedding families checked stability of the canonical generator under an enlarged divisor cutoff.
